erros.devolutiva: Enfatizar que o denominador na reta numérica representa o todo (5), enquanto o numerador representa a parte (3).
Praticar a contagem de intervalos (espaços entre marcas) em vez de contar as marcas verticais.

dicas.texto: Você está no caminho certo! Lembre-se: em uma fração, o número de baixo (denominador) representa o total de partes iguais em que dividimos o inteiro. Quantos livros ela precisa ler no total?
Ótimo! Agora, digite o número total de livros no campo 'Number of parts' e clique em OK para que a reta seja dividida corretamente.
Quase lá! O denominador é o número total de partes. Como ela tem 5 livros no total, insira o número 5 no campo 'Number of parts' e clique em OK.
Você está muito perto! O total de partes é 5, então coloque 5 no campo 'Number of parts' e aperte o botão OK para ver a reta dividida.
Você já dividiu a reta! Agora, pense: se cada parte vale 1/5, onde estaria a marca que representa 3 dessas partes?
Comece do zero e conte os intervalos entre os tracinhos. Onde você para ao contar três intervalos?
Você está indo bem! Conte três espaços a partir do zero. O terceiro tracinho é onde você deve colocar o ponto.
Quase lá! Se você começar no zero e pular três marcas (1/5, 2/5, 3/5), você encontrará o lugar exato. Tente marcar o ponto exatamente na terceira marcação.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; as caixas da fração (F1/F2) existem mas a pergunta da fração não é exibida (a fração já está no enunciado); reta numérica de 0 a 1 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto; campo "Number of parts" (denom) + OK que divide a reta em partes iguais (começa em 1); botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, dividir a reta, marcar o ponto, concluir).

campo numérico "Number of parts" + botão OK: divide a reta em partes iguais
botão que registra a fração informada
controle que exibe a etapa de escrever a fração

passos.acao: Enter the denominator of the fraction shown in the lower box F2.
Enter the number of equal parts and press OK to divide the number line.
Enter the numerator of the fraction shown in the upper box F1.
Mark the point for the fraction 3/5 on the divided number line.
Press the showAnswer control to register the fraction shown by your point.
After checking that the point is right of one-half, press Done.

dicas.texto: Look at the bottom number of the fraction. It tells how many equal parts make the whole assignment.
Read the fraction from top to bottom and identify the number below the fraction bar.
The fraction has 3 on top and a different number below it. Enter the lower number in F2.
Use the total number of books in the assignment as the denominator, then enter that number in F2.
The denominator tells how many equal intervals should make up the whole number line from 0 to 1.
Use the denominator as the number of parts, type it in the Number of parts field, and then press OK.
The assignment has five books in total, so the whole line must be split into five equal intervals.
Type the total number of equal parts represented by the denominator, then press OK to apply the division.
The numerator tells how many equal parts Sally has completed.
Look at the number above the fraction bar and enter that number in F1.
Sally has already read the number of books shown at the top of the fraction.
Enter the number of books Sally has read in the upper fraction box F1.
A fraction on the number line shows how many equal intervals are counted from zero.
Start at 0 and count intervals toward 1 using the numerator as the number of intervals.
The line has five equal intervals. Count three spaces from 0, not three vertical marks.
Starting at zero, move through three equal spaces and place the point at the end of the third space.
Connect the point's position with the number of equal parts counted from zero.
Check the numerator by counting intervals from zero and check the denominator by counting all equal intervals.
Your point should be three intervals from 0 on a line divided into five equal parts.
Verify the fraction represented by the point, then use showAnswer to register that fraction.
Compare the marked point with the halfway point between 0 and 1.
Locate one-half at the center of the number line and observe which side contains the marked point.
The marked point should be slightly to the right of the center because three fifths is greater than one-half.
Once the point is visibly to the right of the midpoint, press Done to submit the completed comparison.

exercicio.statement:
Sally has to read 5 books for her summer assignment. So far, she has read 3 of the books. That is 3/5 of the assignment, and she is convinced that she has read a little more than half of the entire summer assignment. Use the number line to show how much she has read and see if she has actually read a little more than  half of her summer assignment.
-

Enter the number of equal parts and press OK to divide the number line.
Enter the numerator of the fraction shown in the upper box F1.
Mark the point for the fraction 3/5 on the divided number line.
Press the showAnswer control to register the fraction shown by your point.
After checking that the point is right of one-half, press Done.

hints.message: Look at the bottom number of the fraction. It tells how many equal parts make the whole assignment.
Read the fraction from top to bottom and identify the number below the fraction bar.
The fraction has 3 on top and a different number below it. Enter the lower number in F2.
Use the total number of books in the assignment as the denominator, then enter that number in F2.

nodes.description: Enter the number of equal parts and press OK to divide the number line.
nodes.instruction: Enter the number of equal parts and press OK to divide the number line.

hints.message: The denominator tells how many equal intervals should make up the whole number line from 0 to 1.
Use the denominator as the number of parts, type it in the Number of parts field, and then press OK.
The assignment has five books in total, so the whole line must be split into five equal intervals.
Type the total number of equal parts represented by the denominator, then press OK to apply the division.

misconceptions.description: O aluno usa a quantidade lida (3) como o total de partes da reta, ignorando o total de livros (5).
misconceptions.feedback: You used the number of books Sally has read as the number of parts. The line represents the whole assignment, so its equal parts must match the total number of books.

misconceptions.description: O aluno calcula quantos faltam ler e usa esse valor como denominador.
misconceptions.feedback: You used the number of books still left to read. The denominator represents the whole assignment, not only the remaining books.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator of the fraction shown in the upper box F1.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator of the fraction shown in the upper box F1.

hints.message: The numerator tells how many equal parts Sally has completed.
Look at the number above the fraction bar and enter that number in F1.
Sally has already read the number of books shown at the top of the fraction.
Enter the number of books Sally has read in the upper fraction box F1.

nodes.description: Mark the point for the fraction 3/5 on the divided number line.
nodes.instruction: Mark the point for the fraction 3/5 on the divided number line.

hints.message: A fraction on the number line shows how many equal intervals are counted from zero.
Start at 0 and count intervals toward 1 using the numerator as the number of intervals.
The line has five equal intervals. Count three spaces from 0, not three vertical marks.
Starting at zero, move through three equal spaces and place the point at the end of the third space.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta as marcas em vez dos intervalos, resultando em um erro de 'um a menos'.
misconceptions.feedback: You stopped one interval too early. Begin at 0 and count the spaces between marks until you have counted three intervals.

misconceptions.description: O aluno ignora a fração específica e marca na metade da reta por ser uma referência familiar.
misconceptions.feedback: You marked the familiar halfway point instead of the fraction shown. Locate the third of the five equal intervals.

nodes.description: Press the showAnswer control to register the fraction shown by your point.
nodes.instruction: Press the showAnswer control to register the fraction shown by your point.

hints.message: Connect the point's position with the number of equal parts counted from zero.
Check the numerator by counting intervals from zero and check the denominator by counting all equal intervals.
Your point should be three intervals from 0 on a line divided into five equal parts.
Verify the fraction represented by the point, then use showAnswer to register that fraction.

nodes.description: After checking that the point is right of one-half, press Done.
nodes.instruction: After checking that the point is right of one-half, press Done.

hints.message: Compare the marked point with the halfway point between 0 and 1.
Locate one-half at the center of the number line and observe which side contains the marked point.
The marked point should be slightly to the right of the center because three fifths is greater than one-half.
Once the point is visibly to the right of the midpoint, press Done to submit the completed comparison.
